walkthroughs.body_html:
Core Content: The 19th Century 1848-1914 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Core Content: The 19th Century 1848-1914 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Core Content: The 19th Century 1848-1914.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who engineered the unification of Germany completed in 1871?
options: Bismarck
Garibaldi
Napoleon III
Metternich
Liberal and nationalist uprisings across Europe
A war between Britain and France
The unification of Germany
A communist revolution in Russia

mcqs.q: What was the Scramble for Africa?
options: The rapid European partition of Africa
An African invasion of Europe
A trade agreement
The end of empire

mcqs.q: What did the alliance system increase the danger of?
options: A general European war
A famine
The end of monarchy
A peaceful united Europe
The 1848 revolutions united Germany straight away.
The 1848 revolutions immediately created democratic states across Europe.
Most failed in the short term as rulers regained control, but they spread liberal and nationalist ideas that shaped later unifications.
The war was caused by the Scramble for Africa only.
Germany was unified peacefully by a popular vote.
The war was caused by the Scramble for Africa only.
Bismarck's Prussia used a series of wars and skilful diplomacy to draw the German states together under Prussian leadership.
Germany was unified by Garibaldi.

mcqs.q: Did one single cause start the First World War?
options: The assassination of Franz Ferdinand alone caused the war.
The war was caused by the Scramble for Africa only.
The 1848 revolutions united Germany straight away.
No — long-term tensions of militarism, alliances, imperialism and nationalism combined, with the 1914 assassination as the trigger.
